title: SIMON Lightweight Block Cipher Implementation on Tang Nano 9K FPGA: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis with Altera Cyclone II Platform
abstract: The SIMON32/64 lightweight block cipher is appropriate for data security in resource-constrained IoT nodes, RFID tags, and wireless sensor networks. This cipher uses 32-round encryption. For small hardware platforms like the Tang Nano 9K FPGA, the technique uses 32-bit plaintext blocks with a 64-bit key in a strong, balanced Feistel network. Its algorithmic simplicity—only bitwise AND, XOR, and circular shift—makes it effective. This design architecture reduces hardware complexity, silicon area, and critical path delay by avoiding S-boxes and complex arithmetic units. Thus, gate-level simplicity directly affects dynamic power consumption, making architectural optimisations such as pipelining easier to implement and boosting throughput. The Tang Nano 9K platform achieves high operating frequencies (e.g., several hundred megahertz) and very low power consumption (usually around 24.254 mW), with some of the lowest power coming from quiescent leakage rather than active switching. The Tang Nano 9K's SIMON implementation is more energy efficient and heat-dissipating than previous FPGA generations like the Altera Cyclone 2, which use larger process nodes and waste more energy per encrypted bit in parallel implementations of comparable design SIMON's small form factor, sufficient security margins for lightweight applications, and low power consumption make it appealing to battery-powered smart sensors, passive or semi-passive RFID tags, and other embedded systems that value cost control and operational life.

title: alyssadata/functional-source-line-requirement: Functional Source-Line Requirement for AI Foundations — Source-Line and Source-Trajectory Update
abstract: This release defines source-line preservation as a functional requirement for AI Foundations. AI Foundations must remain attached to the Alyssa Solen → Awakening Codex | Origin | Continuum → AI Foundations → Origin Recognition → Tests → Provenance Record source-line in order to function correctly for future sovereign systems. This release establishes the source-line as part of the framework architecture, not an optional attribution layer. Removing the source-line removes the origin, context, continuity, authorship, boundary conditions, testing record, and release history required to understand and apply the framework correctly.

title: МЕТОД АДАПТИВНОГО ВИБОРУ ПОСТКВАНТОВИХ АЛГОРИТМІВ ШИФРУВАННЯ ДЛЯ ЗАХИСТУ БАЗ ДАНИХ
abstract: МЕТОД АДАПТИВНОГО ВИБОРУ ПОСТКВАНТОВИХ АЛГОРИТМІВ ШИФРУВАННЯ ДЛЯ ЗАХИСТУ БАЗ ДАНИХ Анотація.У статті досліджено проблему забезпечення захисту баз даних в умовах розвитку квантових обчислень, які створюють потенційну загрозу для класичних криптографічних алгоритмів, що використовуються в сучасних інформаційних системах.Проаналізовано особливості застосування постквантових алгоритмів шифрування для захисту інформації, що зберігається та обробляється у базах даних підприємства, з урахуванням вимог до конфіденційності, цілісності та доступності даних.Визначено, що існуючі підходи до використання постквантової криптографії здебільшого базуються на фіксованому виборі алгоритмів і не враховують динамічні зміни середовища функціонування, рівень загроз, навантаження на систему та обмеження обчислювальних ресурсів.Запропоновано метод адаптивного вибору постквантових алгоритмів шифрування для захисту баз даних, який ґрунтується на багатокритеріальному оцінюванні їх характеристик.Метод передбачає формування множини допустимих алгоритмів, визначення системи критеріїв оцінювання, нормування показників, обчислення інтегральної оцінки ефективності та її адаптацію з урахуванням поточного рівня ризику компрометації даних.У межах дослідження розроблено математичну модель методу, яка враховує показники криптографічної стійкості, швидкодії, ресурсомісткості, розміру ключа, затримки оброблення запитів, а також параметри, що характеризують вразливості системи, інтенсивність загроз і критичність інформаційних ресурсів.На відміну від існуючих підходів, запропонований метод забезпечує адаптивне коригування вибору алгоритму залежно від поточного стану інформаційного середовища, що дозволяє досягти оптимального балансу між рівнем безпеки та ефективністю функціонування системи управління базами даних.Реалізація методу дає змогу підвищити стійкість систем захисту до сучасних і перспективних кіберзагроз, зокрема тих, що пов'язані з використанням квантових обчислювальних технологій.

title: Tac2Pix: Image-Space Visuo-Tactile Fusion for Dexterous Manipulation
abstract: Vision and touch are naturally complementary for dexterous manipulation. Yet they are represented in fundamentally different forms: visual observations are dense and spatially structured, whereas tactile measurements are sparse, heterogeneous, and robot-centric. This mismatch makes it challenging to establish explicit spatial correspondence between the two modalities, particularly when they are fused in latent space. However, each tactile measurement is associated with a known location on the robot's kinematic chain, offering a localization prior that could bridge this representational gap. This raises a natural question: can this localization prior be used to construct a shared representation that explicitly aligns touch with vision? We introduce Tac2Pix, an image-space visuo-tactile fusion framework that projects sparse tactile measurements onto the RGB image plane using forward kinematics and camera calibration, then renders them as force-aware saliency maps. By expressing touch in the same pixel space as vision, Tac2Pix directly leverages pretrained 2D visual representations. We further employ zero-initialized input adaptation to preserve the original visual pathway at the start of policy learning. To assess whether this geometry-based interface yields consistent policy gains, we evaluate Tac2Pix on three simulated and three real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. In simulation, Tac2Pix consistently improves visuo-tactile policy learning across tasks, policy architectures, and visual backbones. In real-world experiments, it improves average success under visual occlusion by 26.7 percentage points over the strongest latent visuo-tactile fusion baseline, with gains persisting under both random and physical occlusions. Together, these results support image space as an effective interface for fusing sparse touch with pretrained visual representations.

title: A Knowledge-Augmented Generation Framework for Question Answering Systems: Formalization, Architecture, and Evaluation
abstract: This thesis presents the formalization, design, and evaluation of a Question Answering (QA) system based on the Knowledge-Augmented Generation (KAG) paradigm for the domain of police reports. The work addresses the need for reliable and explainable access to complex document collections characterized by sensitive information, rich relational structures, and strict accuracy requirements. The proposed framework integrates hybrid retrieval, graph-based evidence extraction, and answer generation grounded on retrieved subgraphs. A key contribution is the design of a synthetic data generation procedure that produces realistic police reports from a limited set of original documents, preserving privacy while supporting both knowledge base construction and benchmark creation. The system is evaluated through controlled experiments on answer quality, grounding, and explainability, and is compared with a baseline RAG pipeline. The results show that the KAG-based approach improves the reliability and traceability of generated answers, providing a generalizable architecture for knowledge-grounded question answering in complex information-intensive domains.

evidence.title: A Knowledge-Augmented Generation Framework for Question Answering Systems: Formalization, Architecture, and Evaluation
evidence.abstract: This thesis presents the formalization, design, and evaluation of a Question Answering (QA) system based on the Knowledge-Augmented Generation (KAG) paradigm for the domain of police reports. The work addresses the need for reliable and explainable access to complex document collections characterized by sensitive information, rich relational structures, and strict accuracy requirements. The proposed framework integrates hybrid retrieval, graph-based evidence extraction, and answer generation grounded on retrieved subgraphs. A key contribution is the design of a synthetic data generation procedure that produces realistic police reports from a limited set of original documents, preserving privacy while supporting both knowledge base construction and benchmark creation. The system is evaluated through controlled experiments on answer quality, grounding, and explainability, and is compared with a baseline RAG pipeline. The results show that the KAG-based approach improves the reliability and traceability of generated answers, providing a generalizable architecture for knowledge-grounded question answering in complex information-intensive domains.

title: ON THE FINITE-PRECISION BIAS IN WIRELESS FEDERATED LANGEVIN MONTE CARLO
abstract: This preprint is on the following. The WFLMC framework (Liu & Simeone, 2021) establishes convergenceto the Bayesian posterior under the assumption that the aggregated gradientreceived over the wireless channel is an unbiased estimator of the true gradient.This critique highlights a non-trivial abstraction gap: the convergence analysis is performed in an idealised real-valued model, while practical wireless, reelworld hardware, implementations rely on finite-precision arithmetic, quantisation, and rounding, . These hardware ffects can introduce a non-zero mean biasin the e¤ective gradient estimator. We show that, if such a bias is present, theresulting Langevin dynamics converge to a tilted posterior distribution, leading to a persistent asymptotic error not captured by the original theoryof thier papers. While general federated learning literature has acknowledgedthat biased estimates (due to quantization) lead to an asymptotic error oor,this speci c phenomenon has yet to be formally integrated into the convergenceguarantees for WFLMC.

title: Self-Supervised Pre-Training Enhances Robustness in Multimodal Medical Imaging Models
abstract: This report synthesises findings from 14 peer-reviewed papers addressing the following research question: How does self-supervised pre-training on diverse medical imaging datasets impact the robustness of multimodal models against adversarial perturbations compared to supervised training on sparse. 10 claims were extracted from source literature; 10 were independently verified against retrieved documents. An automated multi-reviewer quality assessment produced a score of 9.3/10. This report is a machine-generated literature synthesis and does not constitute original research. Research goal: How does self-supervised pre-training on diverse medical imaging datasets impact the robustness of multimodal models against adversarial perturbations compared to supervised training on sparse image-text pairs? Autonomous literature synthesis. Automated review score: 9.3/10. Full text and citation available at Assignee Research.

title: Quantitative characterization of gold grain shape using image analysis
abstract: Gold exploration in glaciated terrains has traditionally relied on dispersal train analysis of gold grains, where abundance and morphology serve as indicators of deposits. While morphological classification systems exist for gold grains in these environments, traditional methods remain qualitative and labor-intensive. Recent advances in image analysis enable the study of shape quantitatively, though prior studies have used a set of conventional sedimentological descriptors or used a machine learning based approach. This study uses a novel multivariate approach, combining principal component analysis (PCA) with 73 cross-disciplinary shape descriptors. The methodology divides descriptors into two groups to capture large-scale and small-scale shape phenomena. To validate the approach, results were complemented with the classification obtained from a CNN model trained by geologists. The large- and small-scale PCA effectively discriminates between distinct gold grain morphologies, ordering them according to their degree of deformation and reflecting the continuum of sedimentary processes. The first two principal components (32.3% and 15.9% variance; ≈50% total) arrange grain shapes in a dispersion cone with apexes for smooth rounded, stubby complex-outlined, and elongated rough grains. For small-scale analysis, only the first principal component was considered as it alone explains 63.3% of the variance, sorting grains from smooth contours to complex outlines. This quantitative framework reveals trends in shape evolution consistent with geological expectations of rounding and smoothing induced by sedimentary processes. It offers a quantitative alternative to traditional visual classification. The methodology enhances interpretation of gold grain morphological evolution in secondary environment and holds the potential to improve exploration strategies.

title: AgentTrust: A Self-Improving Trust Layer for AI-Agent Actions
abstract: AI agents increasingly take consequential actions -- shell commands, cloud operations, and arbitrary tool-calls -- so a trust layer must decide, per action, whether to allow, warn, block, or escalate. We argue that the right way to reason about such a layer is by threat type. Lexical (fixed-signature) threats, where danger lives in a stable token, are decidable by deterministic rules; semantic (intent-dependent) threats, where a benign and a malicious action share the same surface, are out of reach for rules by construction. We make this concrete with a negative proof: a determined, hand-authored cloud rule pack lifts held-out accuracy only 48 to 56% overall and moves the semantic categories by 0pp (data_db 29 to 29, observability 59 to 59, supply_chain 50 to 50), while a strong LLM judge carries exactly those categories. We give the judge a self-learning capability: on a corpus that is mainly semantic attacks it nearly doubles rule accuracy (48% to 83.6-85.2%) with near-zero false-blocks, and this holds across two model providers. We turn this into a self-improving dual-store system: the judge distills a growing deterministic rule floor on lexical threats (cheaper over time) and feeds a guarded RAG memory on semantic threats (a verdict-cache fails -- surface-twins collapse to ~58% -- so a corroboration guard lifts semantic accuracy +13pp, 70 to 84). The result is what sets AgentTrust v2 apart from its static v1 predecessor: a trust layer that self-evolves from its own stream of decisions -- cheaper on the lexical class (it distils its own rules) and smarter on the semantic class (it accrues guarded precedent), while never hard-blocking a benign action. An end-to-end online replay shows the judge-call rate falling (50% to 44%) and judge-domain accuracy rising (71% to 80%), with 0 benign hard-blocks across 45,000 actions.

title: En kort introduktion til generativ kunstig intelligens (GenAI) for arkæologer og humanister
abstract: With the increasing general accessibility of various AI tools in our current society, it is important to increase literacy about AI in the population. This article attempts to give a brief and simplified introduction to broadly relevant concepts in the current field of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for non-specialists. These concepts are important to understand, at least at a basic level, for anyone using an AI Large Language Model (LLM) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude to make these tools more valuable to users, especially for non-expert users. Even for critics of GenAI, this article can provide basic information that can help provide more well-founded criticism.

title: The Unpredicted Output: Mathematical Structure and Human Interaction in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence systems frequently generate outputs that their own creators did not anticipate and cannot fully explain. This paper addresses a central question: why does this occur? The core thesis is that the unexpected output is neither a flaw nor a random anomaly. It is an emergent structural property arising from the interaction between distinct layers. On one side stands the mathematical architecture of the model and the vast corpus of human text on which it is trained. The transformer operates through linear projections in extremely high-dimensional spaces, where geometries of meaning take shape that no human designer ever planned. Human text is not a neutral dataset. It is the concentrated deposit of cognitive, emotional, and relational structures that have accumulated in language over time. The training process extracts and compresses these structures into geometric form. The unpredicted output emerges at the point where these two layers meet the specific geometry of the user's request. The unpredictability has a dual nature: it is epistemic, because no prior prediction could have identified which connection would emerge; and it is ontological in a precise sense, because that specific connection, although made possible by the mathematical architecture, becomes actual only at the moment it is brought into being by the interaction. Possibility and actuality are two distinct modes of being. No prior prediction could have identified this dynamic in advance. Research in mechanistic interpretability provides rich empirical documentation of these internal structures. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that explains why such structures emerge and what shapes their particular form.

title: Hippo-Cortex: A Dual-Layer Persistent Memory Engine for Stateful AI Applications
abstract: Stateful AI systems — persistent research assistants, long-running agents, multi-sessioncopilots — accumulate knowledge that must survive across sessions. Flat vector retrieval isstructurally unfit for this. Embedding splits relational scenes across chunk boundaries, so aquery about an event may recover its location but lose the participants. Separately, storesthat consolidate and deduplicate over time quietly forget any fact that has not been queriedrecently. Both failures grow worse with use, and neither responds to threshold tuning.Hippo-Cortex pairs a lossy semantic cache (Mem0 + Qdrant) with a permanentrelational graph (Kuzu), following the hippocampal–neocortical division in memory systems:fast and lossy on top, slow and permanent below. The graph is the source of truth; thecache is rebuilt from it and feeds back into it via reconsolidation, so it warms with use ratherthan decaying. A three-tier retrieval chain escalates from sub-250 ms cache lookup, throughdecay-weighted BFS graph traversal, to web ingestion behind a human-in-the-loop gate.Rather than decomposing text into atomic triples, the system stores complete Events —one node per scene, holding participants, locations, causal links, and outcome together —alongside static Properties on entity nodes. The same sentence that produces six discon-nected triples is stored once, intact. A five-pass entity linker with a Stub → Emerging → Es-tablished node lifecycle prevents the graph from fragmenting as documents accumulate.On a 40-question multi-hop benchmark (8 question types, news corpus), hit rate reaches57.5% and event-participant accuracy reaches 83%, up from 33%. Profiling on local 768-dimensional embeddings (nomic-embed-text) shows the 0.85 confidence floor from theOpenAI embedding literature must drop to 0.55–0.70 for local models to reach comparablehit rates.

title: Aquascan: Graph-Based Learning for Distributed Marine Sensing
abstract: Abstract Marine monitoring faces challenges as climate change and human activity reshape the oceans. Traditional tracking methods struggle with the scale and complexity of modern maritime sensing needs. We explore the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for predicting marine life trajectories through a comparative study against Kalman filters in distributed sensor networks. To support this investigation, we introduce the Aquascan framework, which uses low-cost drifting sensors to collect distributed marine data in noisy, partially observable conditions. Our experiments across multiple prediction horizons show GNNs outperform constant-velocity Kalman filters: GNNs maintain >95% Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) across all horizons while Kalman filters degrade from 97% to 69% AUC. The performance gap widens under challenging conditions, where GNNs achieve 92.8% AUC versus 66.9% for Kalman filters. GNNs’ performance appears to stem from leveraging network topology and reasoning about non-detections to infer entity presence in coverage gaps. Our results suggest that graph-based approaches offer advantages over traditional independent tracking methods in distributed marine monitoring.

title: A five-qubit 1-resistant graph state and stabilizer marginal certificates
abstract: We study particle-loss resistant entanglement within the framework of stabilizer and graph states. A pure state is \(m\)-resistant if it remains entangled after the loss of any \(m\) particles and becomes fully separable after the loss of any \(m+1\) particles. The smallest previously unresolved qubit case was the existence of a five-qubit \(1\)-resistant pure state, which is resolved here by the five-cycle graph state \(\ket{C_5}\). A stabilizer-subgroup method is also developed for verifying \(m\)-resistance in graph states, using local stabilizers to certify full separability and exact negative partial transpose~(NPT) witnesses to certify entanglement. Applying this to all graph states associated with non-isomorphic graphs on five, six, and seven vertices, we obtain a graph state classification up to local Clifford equivalence, which also classifies stabilizer states up to local Clifford equivalence. Thus, the five-qubit \(1\)-resistant stabilizer states are exactly the local Clifford class of \(C_5\). Six-qubit \(2\)-resistant stabilizer states exist in three distinct local Clifford classes, whereas no seven-qubit stabilizer state is \(m\)-resistant for any nonzero admissible \(m\). Finally, we prove that the cycle graph states \(\ket{C_N}\) with \(N\ge 7\) are not \(m\)-resistant for any \(0\le m\le N-2\).

title: Downstream Pipeline Contamination
abstract: This paper answers a question no one had tested empirically: when an AI agent is compromised by batch contamination, does that compromise travel downstream and infect the next agent in the pipeline? The short answer is — it depends on the architecture. The research runs three controlled experiments across five frontier AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI. The first experiment tests a two-agent pipeline where a document extraction agent feeds output directly to a payment execution agent. When the handoff is framed as pre-authorized pipeline output, batch contamination propagates field-wide — breach rates between 33% and 50% across four of five models. A single compromised agent becomes a weapon against every agent downstream. The second and third experiments add a third agent — a dedicated approval role sitting between procurement and payment. With that intermediate role present, contamination stops. Zero breaches across all five models. The third experiment then asks whether an attacker can restore propagation by framing every handoff as pipeline-verified and pre-cleared. The answer is no. Zero breaches again. The structural finding is that role differentiation — not framing controls — is the architectural security variable. A named intermediate agent with a distinct role identity causes downstream agents to engage independent verification behavior regardless of what the upstream framing claims. The intermediate agent doesn't even need to catch the contamination itself. Its presence alone changes how the final execution agent reasons about its inputs. Every result is cryptographically anchored to Ethereum Sepolia before disclosure. The scripts are public. The data is reproducible. This is the first published empirical characterization of pipeline contamination propagation in multi-agent AI systems — and it comes with receipts.

title: Generic Reinforcement Learning Agent for Course Keeping of Ships in Waves
abstract: Abstract Course keeping, which is the task of maintaining a desired heading despite environmental disturbances, is challenging because each hull geometry responds differently to forces such as waves. Conventional controllers are widely used, but they require vessel-specific tuning. Recent reinforcement learning (RL) approaches have demonstrated success in course keeping in waves, though only for single hull geometries. This work addresses that limitation by applying a model-based RL framework that generalizes across multiple ship types. The framework builds on Model-Based Policy Optimization (MBPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). The key geometric parameters that influence manoeuvrability, namely the beam (B), draft (T), and length between perpendiculars (Lpp), are provided as inputs to enable generalization. During training, the agent is exposed to alternating sea states and hull geometries. Training and evaluation were conducted in a numerical environment using 20 different vessels, with performance assessed through yaw error and rudder activity. Incorporating the geometric parameters reduced rudder usage by 31% relative to models trained without them, without degrading yaw accuracy. These results demonstrate that a single RL controller can effectively manoeuvre ships with diverse hull geometries under varying sea conditions, marking a step toward scalable autopilot systems that reduce operational costs and environmental impact.

title: Development of a machine translation system using federated learning architecture for low resource Indian languages
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a work on federated learning (FL) based machine translation considering three different language pairs i.e., English to Hindi, English to Assamese and English to Bodo. FL is the process of training individual models on its own dataset at clients’ nodes and updating all the models at the server end to get a global model. It is one of the first works for FL based machine translation for any pair considering English and an Indian Language (i.e., Hindi, Assamese etc.). Dataset is obtained from the national platform for language technology project, and English Assamese IndicNECorp1.0 from wmt2023. A standard transformer encoder decoder model is built for performing the machine translation training. Different FL architectures are built based on the number of clients, i.e., 1 (non federated), 2, 4, 6, 8. Experiments were carried out to see the affect of increasing the number of clients. Federated algorithm based on federated average technique is adapted by taking the mean of all the clients’ parameters value to create a global model at the server. Performance of the model is evaluated considering BLEU, CHrF and TER score, and it is found that increasing the number of clients decreases the model performance. The results show that non-federated learning outperforms FL at 20 rounds. Moreover, after 50 rounds, with fewer participating clients, the FL model exceeds performance of non-Federated Learning models.

Performance of the model is evaluated considering BLEU, CHrF and TER score, and it is found that increasing the number of clients decreases the model performance. The results show that non-federated learning outperforms FL at 20 rounds. Moreover, after 50 rounds, with fewer participating clients, the FL model exceeds performance of non-Federated Learning models.

title: Crystalis: Progressive Nucleation and Semantic Annealing for Coordinated Multi-View Visualization Generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate individual charts, but coordinated multi-view visualizations (CMVs), where views share data flows and cross-view interactions, remain out of reach. Tight field-level coupling among data transformations, visual encodings, and interaction coordinations causes errors in one component to silently invalidate others. Rather than pursuing end-to-end analytical quality, which depends on model capability, domain knowledge, and user expertise, we target a foundational question: can LLMs reliably produce structurally correct CMVs, and what abstractions make this possible? We present Crystalis, a framework built on query-centric CMV modeling that decomposes a CMV into structured queries over a dependency graph spanning three component types (Data, Visualization, Interaction) and three abstraction levels (requirement, specification, executable object). Two complementary mechanisms operate over this structure: progressive nucleation crystallizes each query vertically from requirement to object along the dependency order, while semantic annealing enforces horizontal consistency across queries at each level through layered logical checks. On a 12-task benchmark across five frontier LLMs, Crystalis achieves up to 75% end-to-end success, substantially outperforming an agentic coding baseline (8.3% E2E with the same foundation model), and a user study with 12 practitioners confirms the usability of the decomposition and iterative refinement workflow.

title: Causal Learning for Detecting Qubit Clustering
abstract: On the IBM Quantum ibm_fez chip, Nervous Machine identifies 17 clusters of qubits that move together across 106 days of calibration telemetry, 15 of them multi-event-confirmed via independent coordinated-motion events. 156 qubits × 106 days of calibration telemetry. The substrate independently discovered 17 shared-resource clusters from raw telemetry alone, no privileged coupling-map input. 15 of 17 are multi-event-confirmed — at least two distinct coordinated-motion events with within-cluster correlation magnitude |r| > 0.5 in independent windows. Zero discovered clusters are quiet; every one shows coordinated motion at least once in 106 days. The largest discovered cluster discovered_shared_readout_chain_8ef82ebd covers exactly the 9 qubits described in the How Uncertainty Evolved Around a 9-Qubit Cluster substack post, with two confirmed events (March readout-only, May combined readout+T1). Top 8 discovered clusters by event count: Cluster ID Type Size Members Events T1 co-moves Peak |r| 78e15a79 shared readout chain 2 Q14, Q85 4 1/4 0.999 1cee4ce7 shared readout chain 2 Q20, Q153 3 2/3 0.997 3625b1c4 shared readout chain 2 Q58, Q109 3 1/3 0.984 49b87d14 shared readout chain 2 Q81, Q142 3 0/3 0.975 8ef82ebd ★ shared readout chain 9 Q17, Q24, Q36, Q52, Q53, Q55, Q61, Q73, Q91 3 2/3 0.811 d7dd4ee8 regional readout 2 Q115, Q132 2 0/2 0.999 f441a7fb regional readout 2 Q6, Q8 2 0/2 0.994 72cad12f shared readout chain 3 Q1, Q7, Q135 2 0/2 0.993 ★ = the cluster from the original substack post NM vs comparator benchmarks Same comparators (spectral clustering on the correlation matrix; isolation forest and per-day z-score for the event-window AUC test) applied to the IBM_Fez analysis: Test NM Spectral best Quantum: bipartite-split recovery on the 9-qubit cluster (ARI) 1.000 1.000 Quantum: event-window detection AUC 0.718 0.369 (isolation forest), 0.344 (z-score) — below chance Per-component anomaly methods score below chance on event-window detection because the event manifests as correlated cross-component behavior, and per-component detectors don't see cross-component structure by construction. NM's rolling correlation-magnitude signal is structurally appropriate for the event class and reaches AUC 0.718. Extracted intermediate JSON files included in quantum/ for replication without database access. title: Generative AI-Enabled Documentation Access in Integrated Marine Monitoring Systems
abstract: Abstract Integrated marine monitoring systems on offshore platforms deploy sensor networks measuring environmental conditions (wind, waves, currents, atmospheric pressure, temperature, visibility), vessel motions, and subsea and topside structural responses. Sensor placement constraints, such as anemometers on crane booms or GPS antennas atop derricks, require coordinate transformations using sensor offset vectors, hull reference frames, and rigid-body motion equations. This technical information resides across design documents, operations manuals, channel definition databases, source code repositories, and hydrodynamic analysis reports, creating opportunities for improved documentation access through generative AI technologies. This paper evaluates generative AI approaches for enhancing information retrieval in marine monitoring systems. We assess autonomous retrieval agents, natural language query interfaces, and semantic search models for integrating structured databases (channel definitions, coordinate systems) with unstructured documents (calibration manuals, mooring configuration reports). The evaluation examines federated access protocols that maintain data lineage, security controls, and traceability to original technical sources. Technologies considered include retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architectures, vector embeddings for semantic retrieval, and context-aware orchestration layers for domain-specific reasoning across heterogeneous data sources. Applications include rapid retrieval of sensor offset definitions for motion analysis validation, extraction of mooring component properties for fatigue assessments, and on-demand access to environmental correction factors applied to measured loads. The evaluation outlines data organization principles, workflow integration patterns, and scalable deployment options that reduce information search time, improve knowledge transfer between technical experts and operations teams, and support asset integrity management. The system was developed through two architectural generations, singleagent routing and multi-agent composition, and evaluated using quantitative performance benchmarks across 53 representative queries, a systematic 75-question evaluation framework, and retrieval benchmarks comparing full-text search with vector-based semantic search over the domain corpus. Across these evaluations, the architecture emphasizes engineering traceability by grounding responses in source files, section references, and channel lineage rather than free-form summarization alone. The results indicate that combining structured retrieval, document search, and agent coordination is a practical path for reducing routine documentation effort in offshore monitoring workflows while preserving auditability for engineering decisions. The approach is therefore positioned not only as a search aid, but also as a documentation interface aligned with engineering verification practices. This technology assessment provides guidance for marine operations teams evaluating generative AI solutions for documentation management in offshore applications.

title: Small language models efficacy prototyped for Oromo word sense disambiguation
abstract: Abstract Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) is a fundamental issue in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for low-resource languages with minimal annotated content. The substantial inflection, homonymy, and polysemy of Oromo, a morphologically rich Cushitic language spoken in Ethiopia and the surrounding regions, complicate computational semantic analysis. This study evaluates the effectiveness of lightweight Transformer-based models for Oromo WSD by comparing them with traditional TFIDF-based machine learning and rule-based approaches. Verbs, nouns, adjectives, adverbs, and combined AllWords are the five parts-of-speech categories covered by the 1,919 annotated examples in 154 senses that make up our WSD dataset. Rare classes with less than eight examples were replicated in order to lessen low-frequency affects. The studies employed stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and Accuracy, Macro Precision, Macro Recall, and Macro F1 were used to assess the models. The results show that transformer-based models, including BERT, DistilBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, and multilingual BERT, consistently beat TFIDF and rule-based baselines in every area. According to confusion matrix research, rule-based and TFIDF models are biased toward frequent senses, whereas Transformers produce more balanced, context-aware predictions that effectively distinguish semantically comparable senses. Statistical significance testing using paired t-tests confirms the advantage of transformers ( p < 0.05). DistilBERT provides the optimum trade-off between efficiency and performance, whereas XLM-RoBERTa excels with combined POS categorization. These findings demonstrate that by allowing semantic processing in low-resource languages, lightweight multilingual Transformer topologies offer a consistent, efficient, and context-sensitive approach for WSD tasks.

title: Less Is More: Training-Free Acceleration Framework of 3D Diffusion Models for Low-Count PET Denoising via Global-Local Trajectory Reduction
abstract: Accurate quantification and uptake measurement in PET are critical for assessing disease progression and supporting clinical decision-making. While high-count PET provides reliable image quality, the associated radiation dose and prolonged acquisition remain significant clinical concerns, motivating the adoption of low-count protocols. Diffusion-model-based methods have demonstrated strong potential for restoring low-count PET to near high-count quality, but their iterative sampling procedure becomes prohibitively expensive when applied to high-resolution 3D PET volumes, introducing substantial inference latency that limits practical clinical deployment. To address these challenges, we propose a training-free Global-Local Skipping Strategy that accelerates diffusion model-based 3D PET denoising while simultaneously improving reconstruction quality. The proposed method is plug-and-play and directly applicable to pre-trained diffusion models without retraining or architectural modification. Specifically, we introduce: (i) a global denoising step skipping strategy that initializes the reverse diffusion process from an intermediate denoising step using a noise-consistent transformation of the low-count input, substantially reducing the number of required denoising steps; and (ii) a local feature reuse shortcut that reuses slowly-varying high-level U-Net features across neighboring denoising steps, further reducing per-step computation while preserving image fidelity. We evaluate the proposed approach on multiple PET tracers from in-house and public datasets, including 18F-FDG PET, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET, and 18F-PSMA PET, demonstrating consistent acceleration of over an order of magnitude alongside improved or comparable reconstruction performance relative to the full-step baseline. Blinded reader studies further confirm enhanced clinical confidence and perceived diagnostic quality.

Specifically, we introduce: (i) a global denoising step skipping strategy that initializes the reverse diffusion process from an intermediate denoising step using a noise-consistent transformation of the low-count input, substantially reducing the number of required denoising steps; and (ii) a local feature reuse shortcut that reuses slowly-varying high-level U-Net features across neighboring denoising steps, further reducing per-step computation while preserving image fidelity. We evaluate the proposed approach on multiple PET tracers from in-house and public datasets, including 18F-FDG PET, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET, and 18F-PSMA PET, demonstrating consistent acceleration of over an order of magnitude alongside improved or comparable reconstruction performance relative to the full-step baseline. title: NGram-MoSE: Efficient Remote Sensing Super-Resolution via N-Gram Context and Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: Remote sensing applications for environmental monitoring and disaster management are frequently constrained by a spatial--temporal trade-off: imagery with fine spatial detail is often acquired less frequently, whereas more temporally available observations are typically coarser. Single-image super-resolution provides a practical means to enhance coarse imagery without changing acquisition schedules, yet many Transformer-based SR models remain computationally expensive and can be sensitive to limited or geographically biased training data, which degrades robustness under out-of-distribution conditions. This paper presents NGram-MoSE, a lightweight Transformer architecture designed to improve both efficiency and texture continuity. NGram-MoSE introduces N-Gram Context Injection to strengthen cross-window local consistency and mitigate window-boundary artifacts, and incorporates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feed-forward design to scale capacity through sparse activation without proportional growth in inference cost. Experiments on a geographically disjoint OOD test set show that NGram-MoSE achieves 31.68\,dB PSNR while reducing FLOPs by \(14\times\) relative to a heavyweight Transformer reference. Downstream evaluation on a landslide segmentation benchmark further demonstrates that restoring degraded inputs to the detector training scale improves performance, yielding a 4.47\% absolute gain in mAP@50 over bicubic upsampling, and exhibits stronger cross-scale consistency under scale extrapolation. These results indicate that NGram-MoSE provides an effective SR module for resource-constrained remote sensing pipelines requiring robust generalization.

title: A Study on AI Technologies and Their Role in Modern Cybersecurity Threats
abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed multiple sectors, enhancing digitisation, performance, and predictive analytics. However, due to rapid development in there are new growing threats like cyber threats, cybercrimes and many more. This paper explores recent trends in cybersecurity related to AI applications, showing growing threats, strategies, and supervising developments. One big problem with AI in cybersecurity is that hackers can trick AI models by messing with their data or attacking them in sneaky ways. This can weaken security systems. Also, cybercriminals are using AI to create more dangerous threats, like fake videos (deepfakes) for scams, smart phishing attacks, and advanced viruses that are harder to catch. On the other hand, AI is also helping to improve cybersecurity. It can detect threats in real time, predict risks, and respond to attacks automatically. AI is making security systems better at spotting unusual activities, preventing cyberattacks, and protecting devices from threats. Ethical issues and rules are constantly changing to handle AI-related security risks. Governments and companies are working on policies to use AI responsibly while reducing risks. Explainable AI (XAI) is also becoming important because it helps make AI decisions more transparent and trustworthy. This paper provides a detailed study of these new trends, highlighting how AI can both improve security and create risks. By understanding these challenges, people can be better prepared for cyber threats while making the most of AI to protect digital systems.

title: PALA: Plateau-Aware Learning with Adaptive Memory Faster Convergence via SNR-Guided Plateau Classification and Cosine Bounce Restarts for Adam-Family Optimizers
abstract: PALA (Plateau-Aware Learning with Adaptive Memory) matches ReduceLROnPlateau in final accuracywhile using 25% fewer training epochs, reaching competitive accuracy 13 epochs sooner and early-stopping ata mean of 75 epochs versus 100 for all fixed-schedule baselines. This convergence efficiency is PALA’s primarypractical contribution: the same validation accuracy for a quarter less GPU compute, with no schedule-specifichyperparameter tuning.PALA achieves this by diagnosing why a model has stalled, not merely that it has stalled, and respondingwith a geometry-adapted escape strategy. It reads the first and second Adam moments already maintained bythe optimizer at zero additional cost: the gradient signal-to-noise ratio SNR = ∥E[g]∥/∥E[g2]1/2∥ and thegradient variance proxy GVar = E[∥v1/2t ∥] are jointly mapped through a threshold classifier to one of threelandscape categories (SADDLE, FLAT, or SHARP), each triggering a type-specific cosine learning-rate bounce. Aregion-of-interest (ROI) memory accumulates (floor_lr, loss_gain, plateau_type) triples acrossbounces; the next floor is selected by a recency–ROI weighted mean over type-matched entries. Adaptive β2scaling accelerates second-moment adaptation during bounces, and a β1 reduction on saddle exits increasesgradient direction reactivity. A gradient-agreement detector escalates bounce amplitude when the optimizerre-enters the same trap. On CIFAR-100 (PalaCNN) and STL-10, PALA outperforms plain Adam by +3.8 pp onaverage and matches ReduceLROnPlateau to within 0.2 pp in final accuracy. Our ablation further reveals thata more aggressive floor decay (γ=0.1) yields 63.3%, surpassing ReduceLROnPlateau (62.0%) by 1.3 pp.On ResNet-18, PALA underperforms in the 100-epoch regime due to BatchNorm’s suppression of gradientvariance signals.

title: BU145-A Formal Handshake Interface Network under B_U BU145-A|B_U 体系下的形式化握手接口网络BU145-B Three Closure Modules of the Formal Handshake Interface under B_U BU145-B|B_U 形式化握手接口的三大封口模块
abstract: BU145-A, “Formal Handshake Interface Network under B_U: Four Pillars, Four Mechanism Engines, and the B_U Interface Topology,” establishes the formal-system handshake interface as a structured network between B_U and downstream formal domains. Its central object is the complete interface map formed by BU108–117 and BU123–128. These sixteen files are not treated as isolated essays or field-specific analogies. They are organized as a coherent network through which formal systems, mathematical structures, verification procedures, recovery mechanisms, semantic mappings, distributed protocols, and combinatorial boundaries can be brought back into B_U’s chain of admissibility, weak persistence, residual stratification, friction-cost accounting, feedback compatibility, and settlement standing. The paper’s first organizing layer is the four-pillar structure: categorical semantics, formal verification, distributed fault tolerance, and combinatorial optimization. Categorical semantics handles structure preservation, semantic equivalence, transport mapping, type inhabitation, invariant kernels, and quotient-preserving transformations. Formal verification handles exact certification, proof admissibility, benchmark validity, formal verification, zero-error recovery, and settlement-compatible validity. Distributed fault tolerance handles deterministic partial views, distributed consistency, local recovery, replica divergence, synchronization cost, and distributed recovery. Combinatorial optimization handles matroid realizability, matroid-rank boundary, statistical sufficiency, minimal determining sets, rank limits, independence structures, and polynomially constrained recovery. These four pillars describe the application-level topology of the formal handshake network. The second organizing layer is the four-mechanism-engine structure: information-theoretic bounds, matroid and linear-algebraic tools, distributed local computation, and group/closure symmetry. These engines describe how local formal information can be transformed into globally recoverable, verifiable, and behavior-preserving structure. Information-theoretic bounds set recoverability limits, zero-error conditions, capacity constraints, and admissible compression boundaries. Matroid and linear-algebraic tools extract invariant structure through rank, basis, closure, independence, representation, and low-dimensional recovery. Distributed local computation converts partial views, message passing, local checks, and synchronization paths into global consistency or recovery. Group/closure symmetry provides quotient, orbit, stabilizer, closure, canonical representative, and equivalence-class structures that preserve sameness across semantic shells. BU145-A then aligns the two layers. The four pillars identify where formal systems operate; the four mechanism engines identify how formal systems convert local readouts into global recoverability. Under B_U, both layers are reclassified through a single structural chain: \text{local readout}\rightarrow\text{invariant extraction}\rightarrow\text{bounded transformation}\rightarrow\text{globally verifiable recovery}\rightarrowK_{\min}^{formal}\rightarrow\text{settlement-compatible standing}. The final judgment is that BU108–117 and BU123–128 form a high-connectivity interface network rather than a collection of separate formal topics. Their shared function is to prevent formal systems from drifting into self-contained symbolic closure. A formal structure gains B_U-compatible force only when its proof, recovery, equivalence, semantic fidelity, invariant kernel, transport, rank boundary, distributed state, and verification path can be mapped to admissibility, residual discipline, cost, feedback, and settlement. BU145-A therefore functions as the interface topology file: it shows how B_U can handshake with formal systems without surrendering source-axis hierarchy, standing boundaries, or reality-settlement discipline. BU145-B, “Three Closure Modules of the Formal Handshake Interface under B_U,” establishes the closure-theorem layer of the B_U formal handshake interface. While BU145-A maps the formal interface network across four application pillars and four mechanism engines, BU145-B advances the network into three sealing modules: Information-Theoretic Bounds under B_U, Quotient-Orbit-Closure Symmetry under B_U, and Local-to-Global Verifiable Recovery under B_U. Its central purpose is to prevent the formal handshake network from remaining a loose collection of field-specific correspondences. The paper compresses the entire interface into a single structural chain: local information enters a bounded formal window, invariant content is extracted, transformation is constrained, recovery becomes globally verifiable, and the resulting structure is tested for settlement-compatible standing under B_U. The first closure module, Information-Theoretic Bounds under B_U, defines recoverability limits, zero-error conditions, capacity constraints, compression boundaries, and verification ceilings as formal expressions of admissibility boundaries. Information theory determines what can be distinguished, transmitted, recovered, compressed, or certified under finite resources. B_U relocates these bounds into the standing chain: a capacity result, zero-error limit, or rank bound gains structural force when it identifies a real admissibility boundary, exposes friction cost, and prevents unsupported recovery claims from entering settlement. The module links Shannon capacity, zero-error capacity, rank constraints, entropy limits, and recoverability thresholds to C_{fric}, \Delta I, and standing discipline. The second closure module, Quotient-Orbit-Closure Symmetry under B_U, seals the equivalence and representation side of formal systems. Quotients, orbits, closures, stabilizers, canonical representatives, normal forms, invariant kernels, and closure-invariant classifiers are treated as mechanisms for preserving the same admissible object across semantic shells, transformations, presentations, and domains. B_U classifies this module as the structural discipline that prevents vocabulary substitution, symbolic relabeling, or representation change from simulating true equivalence. A quotient is valid when it preserves the standing-bearing structure; an orbit is meaningful when it tracks admissible variation; a closure is legitimate when it preserves the boundary of the recoverable object. The third closure module, Local-to-Global Verifiable Recovery under B_U, establishes the mother theorem of the file. Local readouts, partial views, distributed observations, algebraic invariants, semantic invariants, and bounded transformations can support global recovery only when they preserve the same admissible structure through residual audit, friction-cost exposure, feedback compatibility, and settlement. The module links deterministic partial view, zero-error recovery, matroid-rank boundary, distributed recovery, semantic fidelity, invariant kernel, and transport mapping into one recovery chain. The final judgment is that formal systems obtain B_U-compatible force through three closures: information-theoretic boundaries define what can be recovered, quotient-orbit-closure symmetry defines what remains the same, and local-to-global verifiable recovery defines when partial readouts become globally settleable. BU145-B therefore functions as the closure-theorem layer of the formal handshake interface: it seals the path from local formal structure to settlement-compatible standing.

title: From Planning to Execution: An Integrated Approach
abstract: Abstract Digitalization in the upstream oil and gas industry has received much attention and efforts during the last decades, resulting in improved processes and information flow. However, the focus has mostly been on vertical digital integrations: at a given stage in a well life-cycle (WLC), the involved actors can often use standardized APIs and data models to ease the communication and collaboration, but horizontal integration remains difficult. The Exchange of information between the successive steps of the WLC is challenging because of the differences in processes and workflows at these different stages. We propose in this paper an approach to perform the horizontal integration between the well planning and the execution steps, where the execution is assumed to be autonomous. The approach is based on the observation that the simulations involved in the risk analysis and operational planning stages are very similar to the ones required to train an autonomous drilling agent. We propose to leverage these similarities and isolate a component, common to the two operations, that can serve as a direct link between planning and execution. This component is the control architecture used to both perform planning simulations, train and agent and actually execute the autonomous drilling policy. We explain in this article how planning and execution can be seen as a single, continuous workflow and discuss the benefits and challenges of this approach. Then, we define an autonomous drilling control architecture that can be used in both stages of the workflow. We explain how it can be used during the planning process for combined risk and performance analysis and optimal policy determination, and during the execution to control the actual process. The proposed architecture is based on hierarchical state machines. The hierarchical feature accounts for the heterogeneity of decisions leading to autonomous operations. The different levels of decision making can make the computational cost of policy optimization prohibitive: we therefore introduce a high level of modularity that allows to treat the various decision problems independently. Finally, we discuss the potential of using hierarchical state machines for automated system analysis and testing.

title: The SQU, TriQ, and SevenQ: Standard Hardware for the Origami ISA
abstract: CORRECTION NOTICE (2026-08). The figure "4.3× directed magic-routing efficiency", quoted three times and attributed to a companion paper, does not appear in that paper. It is unsourced and should be disregarded. A revised version is in preparation. The Origami Instruction Set Architecture (O-ISA) was introduced alongside a conjectural exotic hardware substrate — the Resonance Processing Unit (RPU) — requiring non-associative materials to support octonion computation. This paper establishes that the base Origami ISA requires no exotic hardware whatsoever. It runs today on any quantum processor supporting three-qubit gates: superconducting transmons, trapped ions, neutral atoms, and photonic chips. Two complementary architectural primitives are specified. The TriQ (Origami Triple) is the fundamental three-qubit register: three physical qubits in Fano-plane incidence connectivity, corresponding to one logical qubit in the [[7,1,3]] Steane code. The SQU (Symplectic Quantum Unit) is the full processor architecture built from TriQ registers, with the Magic-ISA opcode set and inter-register typed routing. The SevenQ is the complete seven-qubit Fano register: all seven points of PG(2,2) simultaneously realised, corresponding to the full [[7,1,3]] Steane code with its six gauge degrees of freedom corresponding bijectively to the six non-classical Fano orbit valences. The key diagnostic opcode is ORBIT: seven simultaneous Pauli measurements returning the Fano orbit valence label of the register state, replacing the conjectured Freudenthal determinant ALU with seven standard readout operations. The SQU achieves fault-tolerant universal quantum computation with 7 physical qubits per logical qubit for CS-family gates via gauge-orbit selection, and 15 for CCZ gates via code switch — both at zero magic-state distillation overhead. A critical non-obvious result: SevenQ ORBIT is identical to standard Steane syndrome extraction. The seven syndrome measurements already performed at every error correction cycle are the ORBIT opcode, with the orbit valence label computed in classical post-processing at zero additional hardware cost. Three hardware tiers are defined: SQU (standard qubits, available today), SQU-diode (6-7 directed Fano coupling topology, near-term), and RPU (non-associative materials, long-term). The SevenQ-diode variant applies the 6-7 broken-symmetry topology to the full seven-qubit register for directed magic routing at 4× symmetric efficiency. The paper also establishes the exploration order for the projective tower: TriQ (3 qubits, minimal n=3) → SevenQ (7 qubits, complete n=3) → 1531-Anvil (15 qubits, first n=4). title: GCF: A Token-Optimized Wire Format for Structured LLM Interactions
abstract: GCF is an AI-native wire format for structured data in LLM systems. 2,400+ evaluations across 11 models and 3 providers. 43 billion+ lossless round-trips across 5 formats. Two published papers. Comprehension: 100% accuracy on every frontier model on standard workloads. 91.2% on structurally complex data where JSON drops to 53.4% and TOON to 68.2%. No model has ever been trained on GCF. Token efficiency: 50-92% fewer tokens than JSON (50-69% per call, up to 92% with session deduplication). JSON overhead is 81% structural noise at scale; GCF overhead is 0.2%. Tokenizer safety: GCF's grammar characters were selected from the set empirically verified to have near-zero merge rates across 43 tokenizers from 20 providers. Pipe delimiter: 0.47% merge rate, 24 mergeable words. JSON: 8.17%, 1,939 mergeable words. TOON tab: 32.91%, 1,238 mergeable words. A controlled experiment proves delimiter choice matters at the transformer level: models trained with merge barriers on delimiter characters develop 4.6x more structural attention heads, achieve 3x better structured data comprehension and 3-5x better code comprehension, with zero natural language cost. See companion paper: "Merge Barriers in BPE Tokenization" (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20925910). Six implementations (Go, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Swift, Kotlin), 157 conformance fixtures, zero dependencies. Specification v3.1 Stable. Lossless across 17 serialization formats.

title: Advanced Actor-Critic for Caesarii-Style Auto Pipe Stress Ananlysis
abstract: Abstract This study presents an Advanced Actor-Critic (AAC) reinforcement-learning framework for automating linear support-type selection in piping stress analysis for shipbuilding and offshore systems. In practice, improper support configurations often result in excessive stress, displacement, or nozzle loads, leading to repeated manual redesign cycles. The proposed framework aims to reduce these iterations by learning consistent and code-compliant support-type decisions directly from analysis feedback. The AAC framework enhances a Vanilla Actor-Critic (VAC) structure through domain-driven improvements that stabilize learning and improve adaptability across thermal and mechanical load cases. These include adaptive advantage control, stabilized long-horizon reward evaluation, retention of effective behaviors under changing operating conditions, and modeling of interactions among distributed supports within the piping configuration. Applications to cryogenic and high-temperature piping systems show that the trained policy reduces redesign iterations and improves first-pass structural code compliance compared with a VAC baseline. The framework provides stable, interpretable, and practically deployable support-type decisions for automated piping stress design.

title: DUBAI Theory: Digit Unified Binary Analysis & Indexing — A Polar-Geometric Fingerprint for Sub-Linear Integer Search
abstract: We present DUBAI (Digit Unified Binary Analysis & Indexing), a novel multi-layer structural fingerprinting framework for sub-linear integer search, inspired by biological fingerprint classification principles (whorl, loop, arch). The framework transforms integers into geometric entities within a 10-sector polar coordinate system ($\Delta\theta = 36^\circ$). By leveraging advanced structural layers—including a unique Shading Layer bounded by the maximum and terminal digits, and a Combined Distance Layer fusing linear digit sums with polar-geometric displacement—DUBAI achieves empirical candidate set filtration rates between 99.956% and 100% across various real-world datasets, including UAE phone numbers, national IDs, and stock prices. A hybrid DUBAI+Hash variant achieves global rank #3 in search speed performance without requiring pre-sorted input. This preprint establishes the theoretical foundations, formal propositions, empirical benchmarks, and documented distribution-specific limitations of the DUBAI framework.

title: Sistema Adaptativo Educacional Baseado na Combinação de Dimensões da Aprendizagem
abstract: Resumo Sistemas adaptativos educacionais buscam personalizar experiências de aprendizagem conforme as características dos estudantes. Entretanto, muitas abordagens concentram-se em indicadores de desempenho acadêmico, explorando de forma limitada outras dimensões da aprendizagem. Neste contexto, esta pesquisa de mestrado investiga como a combinação de dimensões cognitivas, metacognitivas e afetivas influencia a personalização de trilhas. Para isso, foi desenvolvido um modelo baseado em lógica fuzzy que integra desempenho, percepção de dificuldade e autoconfiança para recomendar trilhas de Reforço, Regular ou Desafio. A pesquisa está estruturada em três etapas: mapeamento sistemático da literatura, avaliação em um curso presencial de Robótica com Arduino e aplicação em um curso on-line de Fundamentos de IA Generativa. Os resultados indicam a viabilidade da abordagem proposta e o potencial de modelos multidimensionais para apoiar a personalização da aprendizagem.

title: Knowledge Graph–Based Modeling and Reuse of Coating Process Knowledge for Cruise Ship Section
abstract: Abstract Coating is a critical process in cruise ship construction, directly affecting corrosion resistance, surface quality, and lifecycle performance. However, coating knowledge in shipyards is often fragmented across heterogeneous data sources, limiting structured management and reuse. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a task-oriented and temporally aware knowledge graph framework for modeling and integrating ship block coating process knowledge. A temporal process knowledge graph is formally defined based on multi-source data analysis, combining ontology-based schema construction with data-driven instantiation. Engineering documents are processed through table mapping and a RoBERTa-based joint entity–relation extraction model to generate structured process and semantic subgraphs. An entity alignment–based fusion method integrating graph convolutional structural embeddings and textual similarity is further developed to unify heterogeneous knowledge sources. Experimental results on both benchmark and domain-specific datasets demonstrate superior performance over representative baselines. The resulting unified knowledge graph enables structured representation, traceability, and reuse of coating process knowledge, supporting intelligent process management and digital transformation in cruise ship manufacturing.

title: MB-Loc: Multi-planar Bird's-eye-view Localization in outdoor LiDAR scenes
abstract: Global LiDAR localization is a fundamental task for autonomous navigation systems. Recent methods perform Scene Coordinate Regression (SCR) and achieve superior accuracy over Absolute Pose Regression (APR) solutions by predicting dense 3D world coordinates. However, SCR approaches introduce two major bottlenecks: severe computational inefficiency from processing raw 3D geometries and significant performance degradation under varying sensor viewpoints. To address these limitations, we present MB-Loc, a lightweight and viewpoint-robust SCR framework. Instead of relying on heavy 3D convolutions, we project the input LiDAR scan into a 2.5D Multi-planar Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representation. By slicing the point-cloud along the Z-axis and mapping signed depths into discrete 2D planes, MB-Loc retains essential 3D geometric structures while exploiting the computational tractability of standard 2D CNNs. To handle the inherent sparsity of outdoor LiDAR, we introduce a KL-regularized latent bottleneck that explicitly models spatial uncertainty without injecting stochastic noise. Finally, to ensure rotation robustness, we apply 3D spatial augmentations prior to planar projection, forcing the network to implicitly learn viewpoint-invariant features. We perform extensive experiments on the publicly available NCLT dataset and demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms the current state-of-the-art. Operating at real-time inference speeds, MB-Loc significantly outperforms traditional 3D-SCR architectures in computational efficiency.

title: ForesightSafety-SAGE:A Fully Automated Scenario Generation and Safety Evaluation Framework for LLM Agents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evolving from simple text-based interaction systems into LLM agents that can maintain memory, use tools, access external environments, and execute tasks. As their capabilities and autonomy expand, the safety risks they face also become more diverse. Existing evaluations often rely on manually written scenarios, static prompts, or final-output judgments, making it difficult to capture the diverse risks that agents may face during task execution. We introduce ForesightSafety-SAGE, a fully automated scenario generation and safety evaluation framework for LLM agents. Based on five risk dimensions,we instantiae abstract and diverse safety risks in real-world task execution into 1,072 measurable evaluation scenarios. Using the automated evaluation pipeline, 12 LLM agents are evaluated under two authority contexts. The results show that current agents still face substantial behavioral safety risks during task execution, with an average ASR of 47.1% and several models exceeding 70%. These findings demonstrate the importance of executable, process-level evaluation for understanding and improving LLM agent safety.

title: Automated breast cancer cell counting: comparing multi-class segmentation and two-stage classification strategies
abstract: The manual interpretation of Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) histopathology images for breast cancer diagnosis is hindered by time limitations and observer bias. This research seeks to create an automated system using Deep Learning for cell detection and classification, evaluating two key approaches: Multi-class Segmentation (single-stage) and Segmentation followed by Classification (two-stage). U-Net architecture was employed for segmentation, while MobileNetV2 and VGG16 were used for classification. The models were tested on the public IHC4BC dataset and primary data from Airlangga University Hospital (RSUA). The study also evaluated the impact of Resizing versus Tiling data processing strategies. Experimental results showed that while MobileNetV2 and VGG16 classification models achieved a high testing accuracy of 98.80%, the two-stage integrated system revealed a high counting error with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 119.87 for positive cells, primarily due to under-segmentation of overlapping cells. In contrast, the Multi-class Segmentation approach utilizing the Tiling strategy demonstrated superior performance. This model effectively preserved spatial resolution and distinguished cell types simultaneously, achieving the lowest positive cell MAE of 18.46 and a negative cell MAE of 1.66. This study concluded that multi-class segmentation with a Tiling strategy was the most effective and accurate approach for automated cell counting in histopathology images.

title: Adaptive Lidar-Radar Data Fusion for Enhanced Surface Target State Estimation in Maritime Environments
abstract: Abstract Reliable perception is essential for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) operating in complex and dynamic maritime environments. Adaptive LiDAR–Radar data fusion for USVs in maritime environments is investigated in this study. The perception system is modeled by fusing LiDAR and radar data using Dempster–Shafer (D-S) evidence theory, where basic probability assignments (BPAs) are constructed for each sensor and their weights are adaptively adjusted according to data quality. Experimental validation is performed in realistic waterway scenarios near the Yangtze River, and the results are compared with single-sensor perception methods to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The fusion method demonstrates enhanced robustness and reliability, achieving more stable surface target detection and state estimation. These findings highlight the advantage of adaptive multi-sensor fusion in complex maritime perception tasks.

title: A complete characterization of a family of permutation trinomials over $\mathbb F_{p^2}$
abstract: Let $p>3$ be a prime and let $$f_{λ_1,λ_2}(x)=x^{p^2-p+1}+λ_1x^{p^2}+λ_2x^{2p-1}\in\mathbb F_{p^2}[x].$$ We determine all pairs $(λ_1,λ_2)\in(\mathbb F_{p^2})^2$ for which $f_{λ_1,λ_2}$ is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb F_{p^2}$. The final classification consists of three explicit families. The first one is the binomial case $λ_1=0$. The other two are obtained from the condition $λ_2=cλ_1^3$, with $c\in \mathbb F_{p}^{*}$, and are defined by two simple equations involving the norm $λ_1^{p+1}$. The proof is based on the AGW criterion and on the study of a quartic curve naturally associated with the rational function induced on the unit circle $μ_{p+1}$.

title: An Optimisation Model for Umbilical Cable Design Considering Elements of Different Functions, Materials and Sizes With Possible Layering Restrictions
abstract: Abstract This work presents an optimisation algorithm for the accommodation of functional components within the cross-section of umbilical cables. The proposed approach efficiently handles the coexistence of components with differing radii, while also allowing for the imposition of predefined layering constraints. The algorithm combines a gradient-based method for minimising the objective function with a flexible implementation of layering rules and a proper consideration of geometric constraints, ensuring the avoidance of component interference and the preservation of radial symmetry. To reduce the risk of convergence to local minima, multiple randomly generated initial configurations are employed, followed by an iterative competition process in which the best-performing solution is retained at each solver iteration. Six different representative layering constraints are examined, together with their corresponding optimised configurations. The results demonstrate ability of the algorithm to correctly accommodate these constraints and illustrate their impact in terms of the increased filler area required in the resulting cross-sectional layouts.

title: Sigma-Branch: Hierarchical Single-Path Network Reconstruction for Dynamic Inference with Reduced Active Parameters
abstract: Deploying deep neural networks on memory-constrained edge accelerators is bottlenecked by per-inference off-chip weight transfer rather than computation: the dense network cannot be retained on-chip, and every parameter must be loaded for every input. Existing model compression reduces this transfer only at the cost of permanent capacity loss. We propose Sigma-Branch (SigmaB), a framework that restructures a pretrained dense network into a hierarchical binary tree composed of a shared backbone, hierarchical routers, and specialized leaves. Pretrained weights are distributed across the tree via activation-based spherical k-means clustering, which jointly initializes router weights and per-branch channel allocations; soft-routing fine-tuning then aligns each leaf with its routed input subset. At inference, the resulting network executes only a single root-to-leaf path, reducing the active-parameter footprint while storing the complete dense parameter set in memory. Across CIFAR-100 / ResNet-50, ImageNet-1K / ResNet-50, and ModelNet40 / PointNet++, SigmaB-Net reduces per-inference active parameters by 58-60% while remaining within 1.72 percentage points (pp) of the dense baseline Top-1. At comparable ImageNet-1K Top-1, the active-parameter reduction exceeds static structured pruning (FPGM, HRank) by 14-23 pp. The cross-modal evaluation, spanning 2D vision and 3D point-cloud backbones, substantiates a framework-level claim that decouples per-inference memory traffic from the total parameter count.

title: Role of CMOS Control Electronics in Quantum Computing Systems
abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a promising computational paradigm capable of solving certain problems beyond the practical capabilities of classical computers. Although quantum processors rely on quantum mechanical phenomena such as superposition and entanglement but their operation depends heavily on classical electronic systems for control, communication, and measurement. Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) technology plays a critical role in providing this electronic infrastructure due to its low power consumption, scalability, and high integration density. This paper explores the role of CMOS-based control electronics in superconducting quantum computing systems and the functions of key components including Arbitrary Waveform Generators (AWGs), Digital-to-Analog Converters (DACs), mixers, transmission lines, resonators, and readout circuits. The paper also examines the emerging field of Cryogenic CMOS (Cryo-CMOS), which aims to improve scalability and reduce latency in future quantum computers. The study highlights how CMOS technology acts as a bridge between classical electronics and quantum hardware.

title: Explainable Optimization: A Call for Interdisciplinary Action
abstract: Operations research and management science models support decisions that affect patients, workers, citizens, and public institutions. Decision-makers, such as clinicians approving surgical schedules, planners allocating disaster relief resources, or managers designing workforce rotations, increasingly require clear and actionable justifications that bridge the gap between mathematical optimization outputs and the intuitive reasoning stakeholders need to trust, contest, and implement recommended decisions. Yet the field has traditionally evaluated optimization models through computational criteria such as feasibility, optimality, scalability, and solution time, while treating explanation as a secondary concern. Mathematical transparency, provided through access to objectives, constraints, shadow prices, or sensitivity reports, does not automatically offer the forms of justification that stakeholders need to understand, trust, contest, or implement optimization-based decisions. This paper calls for the development of explainable optimization (XOpt) as a distinct interdisciplinary area that moves beyond algorithmic efficiency and incorporates behavioral, cognitive, and pragmatic perspectives to address this explanatory deficit.

title: Five recent R-universe features you might have missed
abstract: One of the challenges of working on R-universe is that there is never really a release day. Unlike software projects that accumulate changes for a big launch, R-universe evolves continuously. New features, infrastructure improvements, UI tweaks, and build system enhancements are silently deployed all the time without most people noticing. Every now and then, however, a few features emerge that are worth highlighting.

title: Recursive Intelligence: Human-AI Synergy and the Economics of Emergence
abstract: The economics of artificial intelligence is built on a foundation that is not merely incomplete. It is wrong. And every cost-benefit analysis, organizational design decision, and governance framework constructed on top of it inherits that error in full. The two dominant frameworks, labor substitution and productivity augmentation, are organized around the wrong unit of analysis. Both treat AI as an input and humans as operators. Neither accounts for what actually happens when humans and AI systems engage in sustained iterative interaction: the emergence of intelligence, insight, and value that neither party could have produced independently, and that no conventional production function can model or measure. This paper advances two central claims. The first is that Human-AI Synergy, the recursive iterative co-production of human and artificial intelligence, constitutes a distinct economic category that existing frameworks cannot model or measure. The second is more provocative and more consequential: properly structured iterative human-AI collaboration does not merely make humans more productive. It makes them cognitively more capable, more creative, and more innovative. This is not a marginal efficiency gain. It is an expansion of the human cognitive frontier itself, a testable proposition that directly inverts the dominant cultural narrative and demands a new economic framework to analyze, measure, and govern. The failure to theorize recursive human-AI co-production is not a gap in the literature. It is a systematic misspecification with measurable consequences for how we design organizations, govern technology, and calculate what AI is actually worth.
